assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect revealed a new class of quantum matter classified by band topology rather than symmetry breaking, with protected edge and surface states. It is original, conceptually clean and has reshaped condensed-matter physics; it is the kind of 'quantum mechanics still surprises us' discovery I favour.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theory of the quantum spin Hall state and the Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group gave the decisive experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Theory plus experiment fits a three-person prize. Contributions of Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang, Fu and Moore are outside the supplied credit and may be raised in discussion.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in many materials and probes (transport, ARPES, STM); first-principles band-structure calculations predicted and explained candidate materials. The field is mature and the interpretation stable, so recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the credited trio fully captures priority given the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and the 3D topological insulator work of Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore and Hasan.
Overlap with the quantum spin Hall and anomalous Hall entry means the committee should avoid splitting the same physics across two entries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a theoretically predicted flat-band system hosting correlated insulators and superconductivity, and it opened moire and twistronics physics. This is a strong, original and highly influential discovery in 2D quantum materials, connecting directly to the surprise of graphene itself.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle and flat bands in 2011; Jarillo-Herrero's group reported correlated insulators and superconductivity in 2018 and drove the experimental field. A clean two-person theory-plus-experiment prize is possible; whether Bistritzer should be included as third is unresolved, and Cao and others contributed to the experiments.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, and the flat-band picture is well supported by spectroscopy and calculation. The microscopic origin of superconductivity and the correlated states is still debated, so some would say it is slightly early, though the central discovery is solid.
uncertainties: Mechanism of superconductivity and the nature of the correlated phases remain debated.
Credit split between Bistritzer and MacDonald, and the junior experimentalists in the 2018 papers, is unclear.
Reproducibility of device-dependent twist-angle disorder.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, operating at the magic wavelength, delivers fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and opens tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. It is a verified, quantitatively demanding measurement advance with real use.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated early Sr clocks; Ye's group pushed it to record accuracy and many-body-clock regimes. Both names are well supported as a two-person prize. Hall and Haensch were recognised in 2005 for the frequency comb, which is a related but separate contribution.
assessment.maturity: Multiple laboratories worldwide have independently confirmed performance, with international comparisons. The technology is mature and the timing is appropriate.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as an instrumentation advance building on the 2005 comb prize rather than a new physical discovery.
Contributions from other lattice clock groups (Yb, Al+ ion clocks) not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultrasoft pseudopotentials and the projector augmented-wave method made plane-wave DFT efficient and accurate for transition metals, oxides and magnets, and are the foundation of widely used codes such as VASP. The impact on computed materials science is enormous and quantitative, though the prize would honour a method rather than a physical discovery.
assessment.attribution: Vanderbilt introduced ultrasoft pseudopotentials, Blöchl the PAW formalism, and Kresse and Joubert the PAW implementation in VASP, with Kresse also the architect of the code. The three-person set is natural. I work in this area, so I note a possible perception of closeness and would defer on how to weigh it, and Car-Parrinello and norm-conserving pseudopotential pioneers are also relevant.
assessment.maturity: Methods are validated by extensive cross-code reproducibility studies and decades of use. Physics Nobel precedent exists with the 1998 chemistry prize for DFT, but the committee has rarely rewarded computational methods in physics.
uncertainties: Whether a method and software prize meets the physics criterion of a discovery or invention in physics.
Overlap with the 1998 chemistry DFT prize and uncertainty over the precise allocation of credit between PAW developers and code authors.
Possible perceived conflict of interest given my own field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution rests on a clear physical principle, that measurement disturbs quantum states and that entanglement can certify security, and links foundational quantum mechanics to real communication technology. It follows the 2022 recognition of entanglement experiments and fits the theme that quantum mechanics underpins technology.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard created BB84 and Ekert the entanglement-based E91 protocol, a natural three-way split. Credit is unusually clean as protocol invention, though the work is closer to information theory than a physical discovery. Experimental implementers are not in this list.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally implemented in fibre, free-space and satellite links, so the underlying idea is firmly confirmed, but practical security and device imperfections remain active. The idea is mature and timely.
uncertainties: Whether it is physics enough in the committee's view, being protocol invention.
Practical-security gaps and limited deployment.
A closely overlapping entry that adds teleportation exists on the longlist.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature and giant tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions underlie MRAM and read heads and extend the spin-electronics line recognised by the 2007 prize. It is a verified physical effect with large practical impact, which I find attractive.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995, and Parkin and Yuasa/Djayaprawira developed MgO giant TMR in 2004. The proposed trio is plausible but the credit for MgO TMR is shared with Yuasa and others not in the list, and Julliere's earlier work complicates priority.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced and commercialised, theory of coherent tunnelling explains the MgO result from band-structure calculations. The effect is mature and the interpretation stable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may make the committee view it as incremental.
Priority between Julliere, Miyazaki, Moodera and the MgO groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of iron-based high-temperature superconductors in 2008 opened a second family of non-cuprate high-Tc materials with multiband physics, magnetism and nematicity. It is a clear and important discovery in unconventional superconductivity.
assessment.attribution: The credited name is Hosono alone, whose group reported superconductivity in LaFeAsO(1-x)Fx, which gives a clean attribution for the initial discovery. Follow-on groups contributed critical materials and theory, and a single-laureate prize may seem narrow.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly confirmed by many groups and now well characterised, but the pairing mechanism remains unresolved and the Tc ceiling is below the cuprates, which weakens the case for the field's long-term impact.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism is not understood and no application has emerged.
Contributions of other groups to the rapid expansion are unlisted.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory gave a controlled non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, explaining the Mott transition, and combined with DFT as DFT+DMFT it connects model physics to real materials. It is a conceptual and computational advance of lasting value to the field I know.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the infinite-dimension limit, Georges and Kotliar the mapping onto an impurity model, and Kotliar and others the DFT+DMFT combination. The trio is reasonable, but Metzner's role is not supported by the supplied names, leaving credit slightly unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Widely used and validated against experiment across Mott systems, with benchmark comparisons, though quantitative predictive power is limited for some materials. Mature, but recognition may be better as a method than a discovery.
uncertainties: Metzner's decisive contribution is outside the credited names.
Quantitative reliability of DFT+DMFT for real materials remains uneven.
Whether a theoretical method fits a physics discovery prize.
